doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Recordings with Mezz Mezzrow, Charlie Barnet and Bud Freeman
summary: Berger runs through Carter's 1933-34 sideman sessions; Carter has forgotten several, including the Bud Freeman date with Willie the Lion and Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: . . . and talk about . . . oh, before we do that, we’re still working with 1933 and your recordings, and it struck me, we mentioned there was one integrated session of the Chocolate Dandies with that title—anachronistic title, oddly enough; it was an integrated band—and later that year you also recorded with Mez Mezro and his orchestra. I believe that was an offshoot of some grandiose idea he had to tour with an interracial group, which never came to fruition, but this was sort of a spin-off from that. Then you worked with Charlie Barnet. You recorded with him a year later and sat in with his band, playing trumpet.
[unclear], was that one of the songs?
Oh, really? Well, I’ll have to play it for you. You don’t solo, but you’re . . .
Then another session with Mez Mezro and with Bud Freeman, and a little later in 1934, so there was . . .
What did I do with Bud Freeman? I don’t remember ever having played with Bud.
. . . Send in the Vipers and Thirty-fifth and Calumet.
Yeah. I’d forgotten that. I always was fond of Bud, you know.
I think that’s your only recording with him.
Yeah, I think that’s the only . . . I’ve seen him a number of times, particularly when we went to Europe, and I think he was living in England for a while. Yeah, gee.
And that, incidentally, had Willy “The Lion” Smith on piano, which was, I believe, your only recording with him . . .
Is that right? I don’t . . . those at all.
